text:
Emma (support): hey team — customer ShopLan reporting a sudden spike of 502/5xx errors hitting hosted inference in EU (reported ~08:12 UTC). They see lots of SDK retry loops and a billing burst. attaching first log snippet they pasted below. Can we triage? :red_circle:

Raj (eng-sre): noted. any correlation ids or request ids from the customer? also which model/route?

Emma (support): they sent this excerpt: `x-request-id: 8f3c2a9b-9d4f-4b2a-b2f0-7a1c3f5d5f9e` and `route: /v1/completions/redwood-2` — timestamps around 08:11:45-08:14:03 UTC. customer says it started after a rolling deploy earlier in EU.

Liam (eng-runtime): thanks — I'm seeing an inbound surge from eu-west-1 around 08:10. Gateway p95 went from 120ms -> 1.2s and 502 counts jump. quick check of ingress logs: `ingress-proxy | upstream_status=502 | upstream_error="auth: token validation timeout"` — looks auth-related, maybe backend auth service slow.

Kevin (eng-infra): paging infra-bot to check auth pool health. infra-bot: @here auth-pool-eu CPU at 92% and connection queues spiking.

infra-bot: alert: auth-service-eu pod auth-eu-7f8c crashed (OOMKilled) at 08:09:53 UTC; restart count increased.

Raj (eng-sre): possible chain: auth service OOM -> token validation latency -> ingress returns 502 to client -> SDK retries create backpressure -> additional auth load. need repro steps and temporary mitigation.

Maya (customer-success): customer needs an ETA to share with their SREs. They reported rate-limited retries causing doubled bill for that minute.

Carla (oncall): I'll take lead on mitigation. immediate plan: 1) Scale auth service in EU to absorb retry storm 2) Restart ingress pods to drain bad conns 3) Apply temporary client-side soft rate limit at gateway for repeated identical request ids. executing now.

Liam (eng-runtime): repro steps I used locally to simulate: 
```
# simulate client retry storm
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2","prompt":"hi"}' \
    https://api.eu.redwood.ai/v1/completions &
done
```
Observed gateway returning 502s when auth responded >500ms. Also saw header truncation in connection keepalive logs.

Raj (eng-sre): added grep for the request id across services: `kubectl logs -l app=ingress -n prod-eu | grep 8f3c2a9b` — found matching traces across gateway -> auth -> runtime. auth logs show `token_refresh: failed, redis timeout` at same time.

Kevin (eng-infra): Checking Redis cluster for auth: redis-eu latency spikes at 08:09:20, 99th = 1.8s. One replica was behind and caused blocking calls. I triggered failover and scaled replicas + increased client timeouts to be defensive.

Carla (oncall): restarted ingress pods (rolling) at 08:25 UTC, scaled auth-service to +3 pods. added temporary circuit-breaker rule on gateway: if same x-request-id retried more than 5 times within 30s, return 429 to limit retry amplification.

Emma (support): updated ShopLan: "we've identified an auth-service OOM + Redis replica lag as root cause; we've applied scaling and a temporary retry-limiter. We're monitoring and will follow up with permanent fix. ETA: 60-90m to confirm full recovery." customer acknowledged, asked for logs for their billing claim.

Maya (customer-success): I'll prepare export of the metric window (08:05-08:20) and include token error counts and 5xx counts — also will open a billing adjustment request if numbers show duplicate billing due to retries.

Liam (eng-runtime): follow-up debug artifacts: 
- ingress tail: `2026-06-05T08:11:50Z ingress-proxy request_id=8f3c2a9b upstream_status=502 upstream_err="auth: token validation timeout"`
- auth logs: `2026-06-05T08:09:53Z auth-service ERROR token_check redis_timeout key=session:tk:abc123`
- redis metrics: `redis-eu-01 avg_latency_ms 1800`

Raj (eng-sre): created ticket INF-3427 for permanent mitigation: ensure auth service has headroom, switch token validation to non-blocking local cache fallback, and add per-client backpressure at gateway. Assigned to eng-runtime + eng-infra.

Kevin (eng-infra): rolling-verified: redis replica resynced, CPU normalized. no OOMs since scale up.

Carla (oncall): monitoring: 5xx counts in EU returned to baseline by 08:48 UTC. p95 latency back to ~140ms. leaving circuit-breaker active for 2h.

Emma (support): customer update sent at 08:50 UTC: "Issue mitigated; auth scaling and gateway safeguards applied; we're investigating root cause and will follow up with permanent fixes. We're also reviewing traffic/billing impact for the window you noted." they asked for a postmortem; Maya to coordinate.

Maya (customer-success): drafting customer-facing writeup now. will CC legal for billing adj if needed.

Liam (eng-runtime): quick note — found one small bug where long auth header (jwt ~4k) was causing `http_parser` buffer reallocation thrash under high concurrency; added a safe-guard to drop very large headers earlier in the pipeline (hotfix PR linked).

Raj (eng-sre): thumbs up on hotfix, please link PR in INF-3427.

Emma (support): final: marking support thread as 'monitoring' and will close when customer confirms billing review. thank you everyone :pray: 

Carla (oncall): closing ops loop in 2h unless new alerts. :white_check_mark:
